correctness.rationale: For D>0 the phase at first passage of successive spatial levels is a homogeneous Markov chain, as in first-passage ladder theory; solving D K² − v diag(1,−1)K+Q=0 gives a=q/(sqrt(v²+2Dq)+v), b=(sqrt(v²+2Dq)+v)/(2D). Alternating Exp(a) and Exp(b) spatial runs are independent. With a→q/(2v), Db→v, coupling their exponential variables yields Poisson negative-run starts of rate q/(2v) and Exp(v) marks for widths/D; boundary-straddling events vanish. FK eigenvalue analysis or exponential-interval bounds yield compound-Poisson Laplace and moment convergence. Independent floating-point Riccati checks and transformed Laplace limits corroborate the formulas.
